main_text.p: postquam accepit, gratias egit, & dedit discipulis, subiecit, Edite, panè intelligens: & paulò post, Bibite, de vino loquens. Reliqua omnia quæ his ad-iuncta sunt verba, ad mysterij expli-cationem pertinent. primùm enim, quidnam visibilia elementa, panis & vinum, fidelibus esse debeat indicat istis verbis, Hoc est corpus meum, Hic est sanguis meus. Deinde, quid actiones e-dendi & bibendi conducat, admonet, dicendo, Facite hoc in mei memoriā. Quid ergo est commemorandum in actione coenæ mysticæ? hoc nempe, Christi corpus pro nobis traditum, esse nobis panem illum de cœlo, qui dat vitam mundo, &c. sanguinem Christi pro nobis effusum in remissionem peccatorum, esse potum illum cœlestem, qui sitientes iustitiam ita reficiat ut sitire desinant. page.notes: The page number at the head is printed in an old form that could also be read as "s2"; I have read it as 52 with some doubt. The word "moratio" at the right is the second half of "commemoratio", split at the line end, and is given here as the catchword. The text itself ends on "comme". The side margins contain only show-through and the edge of the neighbouring page, which I have left out.
